title: Chirped Bragg Stack for Broadened Reflection Band
scientific_hypothesis: A chirped Bragg stack with gradually increasing layer thicknesses will broaden the 400-700 nm reflection band compared to uniform quarter-wave design, improving solar background rejection across the full visible spectrum.
design_principle: Chirped structures (varying period through the stack) create multiple overlapping bandgaps, broadening the reflection band. L06 mentions thickness-modulated multilayer filters for spectral shaping. This addresses the challenge of covering 400-700 nm (300 nm bandwidth) with a single periodic design.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (10 pairs, 20 layers total, with linear thickness chirp)
design_variables: chirp rate (thickness gradient factor across the 10 pairs), base quarter-wave wavelength
soft_objectives: Maximize average reflectance across 400-700 nm band
Minimize reflectance variation across visible band
manufacturing_considerations: Chirped thicknesses must remain within deposition control range
HfO2/SiO2 thickness modulation demonstrated in L06
theory_basis: Thickness gradient creates wavelength-dependent reflection zones
expected_advantages: Broader reflection band than periodic design
Better coverage of full 400-700 nm range
L35 sun-blocking filter context supports broadband visible rejection
known_risks: May reduce peak reflectance compared to optimized periodic design
Chirp may introduce passband ripple at 1530-1565 nm
execution_request_english: Design a chirped multilayer dielectric stack with air incidence on fused silica substrate. Stack: 10 alternating pairs of HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) (20 layers total), starting with HfO2. Layer thicknesses follow a linear chirp: each successive pair has optical thickness multiplied by a chirp factor relative to the base quarter-wave wavelength. Optimize the chirp factor and base quarter-wave wavelength to maximize average reflectance across 400-700 nm band while maximizing transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band. Layer count fixed at 20. Materials: hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand).
